tapeLine: Monday 16 November: S&P 500 −1.9% to 7,416.59, its third straight loss; Dow −739.38 to 51,608.17; Nasdaq Composite −2.5% to 24,509.76, per AP close report dated 16 Nov. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell about 5.3% (Xinhua and other wire recaps, 16–17 Nov).
matters:
Monday was a broad AI and chip selloff a day before Nvidia reports. Nvidia fell 4.1% to $156.14 and the semiconductor index lost about 5.3% (Xinhua, 17 Nov). Fed Chair Warsh, opening the Fed’s Productivity and Jobs Task Force conference, described a downside case in which AI returns disappoint, valuations fall and unemployment rises, calling these “illustrative scenarios, not forecasts,” and gave no rate signal (Seoul Economic Daily, 17 Nov). Stocks were already lower before he spoke. The 10-year yield eased slightly Monday morning to about 5.13% (CNBC, 16 Nov).

Today: October retail sales and import prices at 8:30 ET; Fed speakers Musalem, Waller, Hammack and Williams; Nvidia’s fiscal third-quarter results after the close, the first since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. Futures were lower early Tuesday, with Reuters putting S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 E-minis each down about 0.34% at 5:23 ET (Yahoo/Reuters, 17 Nov). FOMC minutes Wednesday; Anthropic’s IPO is reported to price Wednesday 18 Nov, timing subject to change.

alsoOnTape: 10-year Treasury yield about 5.13% Monday morning, down 2 bp, after a Friday high of 5.174%; 2-year about 4.84% (CNBC, 16 Nov). A Monday close was not found from a wire source. Brent crude around $92.30 early Tuesday (TipRanks, 17 Nov). The dollar index was described as near its highest since April 2025 (Admiral Markets, 17 Nov). Gold and VIX levels were not found with a clean dated source.
overnight: Latest confirmed close — Monday 16 November: S&P 500 7,416.59 (−1.9%); Nasdaq Composite 24,509.76 (−2.5%); Dow 51,608.17 (−739.38). 247wallst’s snapshot differs slightly (S&P 7,411.87); AP figures are carried.
Futures — early Tuesday 17 Nov: S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 E-minis each about −0.34% at 5:23 ET (Reuters via Yahoo); TipRanks reported roughly −0.4% across the three index futures.

Nvidia — closed Monday at $156.14, −4.1% (Xinhua, 17 Nov), after $162.85 Friday. Results after Tuesday’s close; Admiral Markets cites consensus EPS of $2.47 on revenue of $108.85 billion (17 Nov). Wire reports also cited new US rules restricting China’s access to advanced AI chips as a Monday pressure.
macro: Warsh, 16 Nov — opening remarks at the Fed’s Productivity and Jobs Task Force conference set out downside AI scenarios (weaker returns, lower valuations, higher unemployment), described as illustrative, not forecasts; no rate signal (Seoul Economic Daily, TradingKey, 17 Nov).
Retail sales, October — due 8:30 ET; forecasts around +0.2% m/m against +0.8% prior, ex-autos +0.4% against +0.9% (Investing.com). InvestingLive lists the headline forecast at +0.1%.

Anthropic IPO — indicative range $70–$78 per share, Nasdaq ticker ANT, pricing reported for 18 Nov and trading from 19 Nov (RTTNews and secondary reports). Valuation and deal-size figures in coverage conflict and are not carried.
flow: Breadth, dealer gamma, put-call and skew are paid data and are not on this page.

regime.tag: Three straight S&P 500 losses, chips down hard into Nvidia’s report, with the 10-year still above 5%.
regime.sizing: Monday’s selloff came with yields slightly lower, not higher; whether today’s retail sales and tonight’s Nvidia print change that is unresolved.

secondOrder: Friday’s weakness was paired with rising yields; Monday’s larger drop came as the 10-year eased a couple of basis points, which points to AI-specific selling rather than rates as Monday’s driver. That is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: The prior brief listed Fed Chair Warsh speaking Monday at 12:00 ET at the Productivity and Jobs Task Force conference. He gave the opening remarks as scheduled (Seoul Economic Daily, 17 Nov).

The prior brief reported futures lower early Monday (Nasdaq-100 −0.79%, S&P 500 −0.25%) and Nvidia lower premarket. Direction held, but the early snapshot badly understated the day: the S&P 500 closed −1.9% and the Nasdaq −2.5% (AP, 16 Nov), Nvidia −4.1%.

The prior brief said how equities would trade AI news against a 10-year above 5% was unresolved. Monday stocks fell sharply while the yield eased slightly. No direction was called, so there is nothing to grade right or wrong.
The prior brief said Anthropic’s IPO is reported to price 18 Nov with trading 19 Nov. That has not happened yet.
